newsitem.title: SPAIN: Endesa shares soar after ratings confirmed.
newsitem.headline: Endesa shares soar after ratings confirmed.

text.p: Shares in Spanish electricity firm Endesa soared on Thursday after Standard & Poor's affirmed its debt ratings and took it off its watch list.
"The rating was very positive for the stock but we have also seen investors selling Fecsa and Sevillana shares and buying Endesa," said one trader.
By 1030 GMT shares had climbed 120 pesetas, 1.45 percent, to 8,400. The Ibex-35 index of leading shares was up 0.51 percent to 4,589.79.

Standard & Poor's confirmed Endesa's AA+ rating on senior peseta long-term debt and its AA rating on senior foreign currency long-term debt, adding that it had removed the company from its watch list.
S&P originally placed Endesa under surveillance over worries of the cost of its offer for a 75 percent stake in regional electricity groups Fecsa and Sevillana.
It said on Thursday, however, it believed the profitability and financial coverage of the group was still strong.
Investor switching into Endesa was partly based on liquidity, dealers said.
"Investors are moving into Endesa as it now controls 75 percent of Fecsa and Sevillana and Endesa is now a more liquid stock," said one trader.
Endesa said on Wednesday that shareholders in the two regional companies had overwhelmingly accepted its offer for their shares.
